connector_package.description: ShipBob REST API 2026-07 (orders, inventory, channel probe) via CatalogRuntimeConnector. Partial migration from retired /1.0 (410 Gone since 2026-08-29). Bulk shipment listing is not migrated; see follow_up_notes.
follow_up_notes: Orders: GET /2026-07/order still takes Page and Limit and returns a bare array. sync_plan stays query_page with page_query_param Page and records_path "". Auth header is unchanged (Authorization: Bearer).

Channel probe: GET /2026-07/channel returns { items, next, prev }. connection_probe.records_path is "items" so required_field id and account_info_mapping read a channel object. The action accepts optional RecordsPerPage (default 50) and Cursor; the probe calls the first page only and does not follow next. Documented next/prev values are URLs (example: "/2026-07/channel?cursor=..."), so the existing pagination type that matches is links_next_query (links_next_path "next", links_next_cursor_param "cursor", cursor_query_param "Cursor") — the same next-link-plus-named-query-param shape as Spotify/Okendo, not cursor_from_body (that would resend the whole URL as the Cursor value). Channel is not a sync_plan entity, so no sync pagination block was added.

Inventory: GET /2026-07/inventory returns { items, first, next, prev, last } and takes PageSize instead of Page/Limit. records_path is "items". pagination is links_next_query (next link in the body; same type as Spotify, Klaviyo, and Okendo — not page_info_link, which reads a Link header, and not query_page). PageSize is mapped from input.limit. The inventory docs show next as a URL but the example value is the placeholder "string"; channel next URLs and ShipBob SDK paging hrefs use a cursor query param, so links_next_cursor_param and cursor_query_param are "cursor". Confirm that param name on a sandbox response before relying on multi-page inventory sync. Published InventoryResponse identifies rows with inventory_id, not id; id_field is inventory_id. schemas/entities/sync-row.schema.json still requires id and is shared with orders and shipments, so inventory row validation against that schema is not confirmed.

OPEN — shipments bulk list is not fixed. GET /2026-07/shipment/{shipmentId} fetches one shipment and is not a list. There is no documented bulk /shipment list on API 2026-07; shipment rows are nested on each GET /order element as shipments[]. Grep of templates/connectors/*/connector.json shows records_path is only a single dotted path (for example "items", "data", "artists.items"). CatalogRuntimeConnector has no precedent for flattening shipments[] out of every order into its own synced entity. sync_plan.shipments pagination is "none" so this package does not keep calling the retired Page/Limit list contract; that is not a bulk sync. Decision for Nate / the connector platform owner: add multi-path records_path flattening, or remove shipments as an independently synced entity and surface shipments[] on orders. Do not treat the shipments entity as resolved.

shipments.open_design_question: Not fixed. GET /2026-07/shipment/{shipmentId} requires a shipment id and does not bulk-list. Shipment data is nested under GET /2026-07/order shipments[]. CatalogRuntimeConnector records_path cannot flatten that nested array into this entity. Needs a platform decision (multi-path flattening, or drop independent shipment sync and keep shipments on the order). pagination none only stops the retired Page loop; it does not sync shipments.
